title: Pupil details: the Enter button
one: Check the four boxes, keep them in Global.cs, switch off the panel.

prev.title: Global.cs: the file that remembers things between forms

stages.title: Check what your Enter button has

screens.title: Check what your Enter button already does
screens.goal: I check that the Enter button has code, starts with string errors, lists what is missing, and switches the panels.

blocks.p: Your Enter button may have some code already. This screen checks what is there.

check.what: In the Design tab, double-click the Enter button. Is there code between its curly brackets?
check.how: The code tab opens at btnEnter_Click. Lines between the curly brackets mean yes.

check.what: Does the first line inside it start with the words string errors?
check.how: Look at the line straight after the first curly bracket.

check.what: Run it. Leave every box empty and press Enter. Does one message list what is missing?
check.how: Use the green Start arrow. Log in first, then press Enter.

check.what: Fill in all four and press Enter. Does the details panel go grey and the attempts panel wake up?
check.how: Grey means switched off. Its boxes cannot be clicked.

screens.title: Start an empty list of problems
screens.goal: The Enter button starts with an empty string called errors, so every problem found can be added to it.

blocks.p: The Enter button checks four things. A pupil could get more than one of them wrong.
So the code collects every problem first. Then it shows them all in one message.

words: Is this box empty, or only spaces?
Or. Only one side needs to be true.
Add this on to the end.
Nothing is chosen in the drop-down list yet.
Switch it off. It goes grey and cannot be clicked.
blocks.intro: Six new things in this chapter. Click any marked word to see what it means.

steps.do: In the Design tab, double-click the Enter button.
steps.see: The code tab opens at btnEnter_Click.

code.title: The Enter button, part 1 of 6
code.where: between the curly brackets of btnEnter_Click, in frmDataEntry.cs
partLines: Visual Studio wrote these two lines
Leave them as they are. Your code goes between the curly brackets.
given
An empty list of problems
errors holds words. It starts with nothing in it. Each problem found is added to it.

blocks.watch: The errors line goes first. Every check below adds to it.

screens.title: Add a problem when a name box is empty
screens.goal: If the surname box or the first name box is empty, a line saying so is added to errors.

blocks.p: The first check asks: is either name box empty?
[[string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace|0]] asks if a box is empty or holds only spaces. [[|||1]] means or.
[[+=|2]] adds a line on to the end of errors. [[\n|3]] starts that line on a new line.

code.title: The Enter button, part 2 of 6
code.where: under part 1, inside btnEnter_Click, in frmDataEntry.cs
partLines: Is a name box empty?
Is the surname box empty, OR is the first name box empty?
Add the problem
A note for you, then a new line is added to errors.

blocks.watch: Two straight lines make or. The key is next to Z on most keyboards. Hold Shift.

screens.title: Add a problem when a name is too long or nothing is chosen
screens.goal: A name over 20 letters adds a too long line, and an empty drop-down list adds a must select line.

blocks.p: Two more checks. Is a name too long? Is a drop-down list left with nothing chosen?
[[.SelectedIndex == -1|4]] asks if nothing is chosen. -1 means nothing is chosen yet.

code.title: The Enter button, part 3 of 6
code.where: under part 2, inside btnEnter_Click, in frmDataEntry.cs
partLines: Too long?
Is either name more than 20 letters? If so, add a line to errors.
Nothing chosen?
Is nothing chosen for year group OR gender? A note, then a line is added.
code.yours: MY longest name is 20 letters. Use the number YOUR task sheet gives.

blocks.watch: Leave the spelling mistakes in the notes. The computer skips notes.

stages.title: Show the problems or keep the details

screens.title: Show every problem in one message
screens.goal: If errors has anything in it, one message box shows every problem found.

blocks.p: Now every check is done. If errors holds anything, there was a problem.
errors.Length counts its characters. More than 0 means something was added.

code.title: The Enter button, part 4 of 6
code.where: under part 3, inside btnEnter_Click, in frmDataEntry.cs
partLines: Any problems? Show them
If errors is not empty, a message box shows every line in it.

blocks.watch: There is one message box, not three. It shows every problem at once.

screens.title: Keep the four details in Global.cs
screens.goal: With no problems, the surname, first name, gender and year group each go into their line in Global.cs.

blocks.p: else runs when errors is empty. That means every box was filled in right.
So the four details are kept in Global.cs. That is the file you made in chapter 3. Every form can read it.

code.title: The Enter button, part 5 of 6
code.where: under part 4, inside btnEnter_Click, in frmDataEntry.cs
partLines: No problems
else, then a note for you.
Keep the four details
Each one goes into its line in Global.cs.

blocks.watch: else opens with a curly bracket here. Its closing curly bracket comes in part 6.

screens.title: Switch off the details panel and switch on the attempts panel
screens.goal: After the details are kept, the attempts panel switches on and the details panel switches off.

blocks.p: Last, the Enter button moves the pupil on. [[Enabled = false|5]] switches a panel off.

flow.before: The details are filled in right. Enter is pressed.
flow.say: The details panel goes grey and switches off. The attempts panel switches on.

code.title: The Enter button, part 6 of 6
code.where: under part 5, inside the else of btnEnter_Click
partLines: Move to the next panel
The attempts panel switches on. The details panel switches off.
Visual Studio wrote these two lines
Leave them as they are. Your code goes between the curly brackets.
given

screens.title: Try every way through the Enter button
screens.goal: I run the program and try empty boxes, a long surname, all four filled in, and typing in the grey panel.

blocks.p: Run your program and log in. Then try each row. A row that fails tells you where to look.

check.what: Leave every box empty and press Enter.
check.how: One message lists every missing thing, each on its own line.
check.fix: Look at parts 2 and 3 on screens 2-2 and 2-3.

check.what: Type a surname of 21 letters. Fill in the rest. Press Enter.
check.how: The message says the name is too long.

check.what: Fill in all four and press Enter.
check.how: The details panel goes grey. The attempts panel can be clicked.

check.what: After that, click in the surname box and try to type.
check.how: You must NOT be able to type in it.
check.fix: If you can, look at part 6 on screen 3-3.
